sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Some druids held a concealment power called druid’s fog. A druid wrapped himself in mist and walked past watching enemies unseen. Irish tradition calls the same power the féth fiada. MacKillop prints druid’s fog as a one-line cross-reference and sends readers to the féth fiada entry. The printed article adds no detail beyond that pointer. The gift could turn its bearer into a veil of mist, much as a shape-shifter takes an animal body. Druids, gods, and a saint all drew on the same mist. Tradition says the Tuatha Dé Danann kept the fog as their consolation when the Milesians won Ireland. St. Patrick also trusted this gift. In the poem St. Patrick’s Breastplate, he and a companion passed dangerous druids. Those druids saw only a fawn and a deer.

okr.objective: Blend the MacKillop cross-reference into the druid's fog entry with modest expansion.
